incentives.name: Data center property sales tax exemption
incentives.what: Exempts data center property (construction materials, equipment, servers, software, and electricity used at the data center) from sales and use tax for data centers built on or after July 1, 2017 with at least 100 MW critical IT load, at least 1 MW per tenant, and $150 million cumulative capital investment, met within 5 years of construction start. Extended in 2021 after lobbying (per WUSF).

dockets.what: Duke Energy Florida petition (filed 2026-04-22) for a limited proceeding to approve a Large Load Customer Policy, Large Load Customer Agreement and revised CIAC tariffs under SB 484 (Ch. 2026-65): customers with forecast peak contract demand of 50 MW+ at one location, minimum term, minimum monthly bill, security, early termination fee, non-refundable system impact fee, 100% upfront line-extension cost; service under GSD-1/GSDT-1 until a new rate class exists. OPC and Florida Rising moved to dismiss; PSC denied the motion (Order PSC-2026-0264-PCO-EI, 2026-07-28). Hearing held Aug 25, 2026; a commissioner wrote it appears 'facially noncompliant' with SB 484. Duke would serve the Fort Meade campus.
dockets.status: hearing held; order pending after post-hearing briefs

dockets.what: FPL compliance filing saying its 2026-2029 rate structure (approved Nov 2025) already meets SB 484: large-load customers fund an engineering study and 100% of new generation, build their own substation, pay upfront for upgrades, minimum bill, 20-year contract and exit fee.
Duke's first large load tariff petition (filed Sept 2025). Abated 2026-03-19 after SB 484 passed; Duke withdrew it 2026-04-20 and refiled as 20260064-EI.

FPL 2025 rate case. Created Large Load Contract Service tariffs LLCS-1 and LLCS-2 (new or added demand of 50 MW+ at one location, load factor 85%+) and an Incremental Generation Charge. The Florida Energy for Innovation Association (data center developers) intervened, calling the LLCS rates and terms excessive. PSC approved a four-year rate agreement on 2025-11-20 (FPL newsroom).
FPL 2026-2035 Ten-Year Site Plan review. FPL told staff it has 32 active data center customer accounts and projects 2 large data center accounts (LLCS, 50 MW+) likely to begin service in 2028.

laws_and_bills.name: SB 484 (2026) Florida Hyperscale Data Center Act
laws_and_bills.what: Signed by Gov. DeSantis May 2026, effective July 1, 2026. Data centers of 50 MW+ peak are 'large-scale'; utilities must ensure large-load customers bear their full cost of service; water-use protections; local governments keep authority to deny or regulate data centers; allows local governments and agencies to sign NDAs with data center companies for up to 12 months; OPPAGA study due July 1, 2027. Final Senate vote 31-6 on 2026-03-13 after the House weakened transparency language.
